title: A spotty wrist
context: A child in North Carolina is feverish with headache and muscle aches, five days after a family camping trip. The rash started at the wrists and ankles.
question: What's the diagnosis?

img.author: CDC
img.alt: Back of a child's hand and wrist covered in small red macules and petechiae.

hints: Ask about ticks. Then ask again.
The rash starts on the wrists and ankles, then spreads towards the trunk, and can involve the palms and soles.
why: Small blanching macules turning petechial over the wrist and back of the hand: a centripetal spotted-fever rash.
pearl: Start doxycycline on suspicion, at any age: delays beyond day 5 sharply raise the death rate, and the classic triad of fever, rash and tick bite is present in only a minority at first. Related rickettsial spotted fevers occur worldwide.

title: Thick yellow nails
context: A 67-year-old who swims at the local pool says his big toenails have slowly turned thick, yellow and crumbly.
question: What's the diagnosis?

img.author: CDC/ Dr. Edwin P. Ewing, Jr.
img.alt: Both great toenails thickened and yellow-brown with streaks and crumbling free edges.

hints: It started at the free edge and is slowly creeping back.
The same organism often causes athlete’s foot.
why: Thick, yellow, streaky great toenails with crumbly debris lifting from the free edge.
pearl: Confirm with nail clippings for microscopy and culture before months of treatment: only about half of abnormal-looking nails are fungal. Psoriasis is the great mimic.

title: The sore that won't heal
context: A 34-year-old aid worker back from rural Afghanistan has a painless ulcer on her forearm. It started as a small bump where she was bitten by insects at dusk three months ago.
question: What's the diagnosis?

img.author: CDC (cropped)
img.alt: A round, crusted ulcer with a raised rolled border on hairy forearm skin.

hints: Think about who bites at dusk: tiny sandflies.
A painless ulcer with a raised, volcano-like rim that slowly enlarges over months.
why: A round, crusted ulcer with a raised, rolled border: the classic 'volcano' sore of cutaneous leishmaniasis.
assoc: Middle East, Afghanistan, Latin America, East Africa
pearl: Cutaneous leishmaniasis is one of the WHO's neglected tropical diseases, with hundreds of thousands of new cases a year. Many sores heal alone over months but leave scars; some species can later spread to the nose and mouth.

title: Look inside the cheek
context: An unvaccinated 22-year-old with three days of high fever, cough, runny nose and red eyes. No rash yet.
question: What's the sign?

img.author: CDC/Dr Heinz F. Eichenwald
img.alt: Close intraoral view of the buccal mucosa with tiny bright red spots bearing pale centres.

hints: They usually appear a day or two before the rash.
Classically 'grains of salt on a red background'.
why: Tiny white-grey spots on red buccal mucosa, opposite the molars.
assoc: Rash spreading from the face down
pearl: Koplik spots are pathognomonic of measles and appear before the rash, fading as it arrives. Measles is highly infectious, so notify public health and isolate.

title: Look at the back
context: An unvaccinated young person, five days into a fever with cough, runny nose and red eyes. The rash began on the face.
question: What's the diagnosis?

img.author: CDC/Dr Heinz F. Eichenwald
img.alt: A patient's back covered in a raised red blotchy rash with merging lesions.

hints: The rash spread down from the hairline.
Look inside the cheek for an earlier clue.
why: A blotchy red maculopapular rash, merging into patches over the back.
pearl: Measles is one of the most contagious infections known. The rash starts behind the ears and on the face and moves down. Two doses of MMR protect about 97%.

title: Itchy at night
context: Everyone in the household has had an intense itch for weeks, worst at night.
question: What's the diagnosis?

img.author: CDC/J. Pledger
img.alt: Back of a hand with small papules in the web space between the index and middle fingers.

hints: Look at the web spaces between the fingers.
Treat the whole household at the same time.
why: Small itchy papules in the finger web space, a favourite site for the burrowing mite.
assoc: Impetigo and rheumatic heart disease risk
pearl: Treat all close contacts at once and wash bedding. Itch can last a few weeks after successful treatment, so it's not necessarily failure.

title: Purple marks
context: A 41-year-old with weight loss, not previously tested for HIV, and painless purple patches on the leg.
question: What's the diagnosis?

img.author: CDC/Dr Steve Kraus
img.alt: Inner side of an ankle with several purplish skin lesions.

hints: The marks don't blanch when pressed.
why: Purple-brown patches and papules around the ankle and foot.
pearl: Kaposi sarcoma is an AIDS-defining illness and often improves with HIV treatment alone. It can also affect the mouth, gut and lungs.
